brief.thesis: Naafiri is a burst-and-reset skirmisher whose all-in lives or dies on her E (Bite) cooldown and how many Darkin packmates her passive has spawned; Sett is a grindy duelist whose W (Haymaker) heals off missing HP, so the matchup is a race between her front-loaded burst window and your sustained-trade window. Whoever forces the fight on their own terms wins it — she wants to open and disengage fast, you want to extend and out-heal.

theirWindow.when: Level 2, right after she lands Q poke
theirWindow.what: She'll chain W (Eviscerate) dash into E (Bite) for a full burst combo before you have W leveled. Play for space, don't stand in the Q dagger cone pre-6, and don't contest CS in melee range until you have at least one Grit-full auto banked.

yourWindow.when: Her E (Bite) is on cooldown or she's used W to farm
yourWindow.what: Walk up and force extended contact — she has no gap-closer left to disengage with, so land your grabbed E (Face Slam), pop empowered Facebreaker autos, and let W (Haymaker) heal you back through whatever Q chip she gets in.

start.why: Negates her Q (Darkin Daggers) poke damage per hit and lets you sit on CS without losing the passive-regen war.

boots.why: Naafiri's damage is almost entirely physical (Q daggers, on-hit W/E), so flat AA damage reduction outvalues tenacity here.

core.why: The proc heals off her burst and the crit-conversion punishes her low base armor in short trades.
The slow from Spellblade catches her mid-dash out of W (Eviscerate), and the extra damage keeps you relevant into a full-build Naafiri.
The shield directly counters her burst-reset combo and keeps you alive through the R (packmate) all-in.

runes.keystoneWhy: You want the fight to last past her initial burst window — Conqueror's ramping adaptive force rewards exactly the extended trades your W heal is built for.

summoners.why: Naafiri has no self-peel once E (Bite) is down; Ignite closes out the all-in windows you win and denies any lifesteal she's built.

playing.title: Manage the wave before E
playing.detail: Face Slam grabs the nearest unit, not Naafiri specifically — if minions sit between you, your pull whiffs onto a minion. Thin or freeze the wave so she's the closest target when you commit.

playing.title: Punish her E (Bite) cooldown
playing.detail: Bite is her only true gap closer besides the W dash. The moment she uses it to poke or reposition, walk up and force a trade she can't cleanly exit.

playing.title: Bank W (Haymaker) for mid-trade, not pre-trade
playing.detail: The heal scales with missing HP, so popping it after eating her burst maximizes the heal-back and flips the extended fight your way.

playing.title: Count her passive packmates
playing.detail: Every kill or assist near her spawns a Darkin packmate that adds real DPS. Check how many are active before diving — a 2-packmate Naafiri hits far harder than a solo one.

playing.title: Threaten first at level 6
playing.detail: The Show Stopper's damage is percent max HP, making it proportionally scarier to her thin frame than her kit is to yours. Look to force the all-in the moment your ult is up if her R isn't.

playing.title: Disengage below 40% HP
playing.detail: Eviscerate deals bonus execute-style damage to low-HP targets. If you drop under that threshold, back off instead of finishing the trade — that's exactly when her W spikes hardest.

verdict.line: You lose if you trade freely into Reckless Swing stacks or engage into an up Ragnarok; you win if you force all-ins at levels 3-5 and again post-6 whenever his R is on cooldown.

brief.thesis: Olaf's E (Reckless Swing) is true damage to both of you, so stacking armor doesn't make trading into him free the way it does against most top laners. Worse, his R (Ragnarok) grants immunity to all disables, which directly no-sells the two abilities your whole kit is built around — E (Facebreaker)'s stun and R (The Show Stopper)'s suppression grab simply fail to lock him down while it's active. This matchup is decided by whether you fight on your cooldown timers or his.

theirWindow.what: Do not commit E (Facebreaker) or R (The Show Stopper) — both fail against his CC immunity and he gets bonus attack speed to punish the whiff. Poke with Q (Knuckle Down) and autos only, and bait the ult out with a half-commit before going in.

yourWindow.what: This is when your grab actually lands. Full commit: W (Haymaker) for the shield and slow, E (Facebreaker) into a wall for the stun, empowered Grit auto, then R (The Show Stopper) to close it out.

start.why: Sustain and early trade damage to survive Reckless Swing pokes before your stun combo is online.

boots.why: Blunts his Vicious Strikes attack-speed steroid and repeated Undertow/auto poke.

core.why: The movement speed and burst spellblade proc let you land the E-into-empowered-auto combo and stick through his Ragnarok speed boost.
The health bar and damage amp are your answer to his true damage — it doesn't get bypassed the way armor does.

runes.keystoneWhy: Sustained stacking damage and heal-back matter more here than one burst window, since Olaf can just out-true-damage a single burst combo — Conqueror keeps you competitive across the whole extended trade.

summoners.why: Ignite directly cuts the Vicious Strikes/Reckless Swing lifesteal that lets him win extended trades, and secures the kill inside your levels 3-5 all-in window before his R comes online.

playing.title: Track his R cooldown, not just his health
playing.detail: Ragnarok makes your E and R whiff entirely. Never commit the grab combo while it's up — poke instead and wait him out.

playing.title: Don't auto-trade through Reckless Swing
playing.detail: His E is true damage on top of his own self-damage, meaning he's willing to burn health you can't mitigate with armor. Disengage rather than match autos.

playing.title: Land E into terrain
playing.detail: Facebreaker only stuns if you throw him into a wall; without one he's just tossed behind you with zero CC applied.

playing.title: Watch for his axe on the ground
playing.detail: Undertow leaves a pickup axe that refunds cooldown — if it's still sitting there, his kit is running on longer timers and he's weaker to engage.

playing.title: Time all-ins to your Grit bar
playing.detail: Once the Grit meter under your health bar is full, your next auto becomes an empowered haymaker — hold the engage a half-second to land it inside the stun window.

playing.title: Don't Flash to chase during his ult
playing.detail: He's immune to slows and gets bonus attack speed during Ragnarok, so trying to stick with Flash just wastes it. Disengage and punish him after it ends instead.

playing.title: Force the level 3-5 kill lane
playing.detail: This is your clearest advantage window before his R exists — commit Ignite-backed all-ins here rather than passing up the lane.

verdict.line: You lose levels 1–5 outright, and you win everything after 15 minutes.

brief.thesis: Renekton is one of the hardest early lane bullies in the game and Sett is one of the better late-game bruisers, so this lane is entirely about surviving levels 1–5. The saving grace is that Sett's W converts damage taken into grit while Renekton's all-in is front-loaded burst — his combo literally loads your gun. Most Setts lose this matchup by trying to trade first instead of letting him commit and W'ing back.

theirWindow.what: Empowered W stuns and deals bonus max-health damage. Do not be in range. Back off, farm under tower, and let him shove the wave.

yourWindow.what: He is one of the weakest champions in the game for those few seconds. Every trade and every all-in you take happens inside this window.

playing.title: Let him commit first
playing.detail: Eat the E-W, bank the grit, then W the true damage back into him. Land the centre of the cone, not the edge.

playing.title: Hold E until his dashes are gone
playing.detail: Facebreaker is your only hard CC and he will simply E away from it. Use it once both charges are spent, to guarantee the W.

playing.title: Ult him through his own R
playing.detail: Show Stopper scales off the target's bonus health and Dominus hands him a large chunk of it. His ultimate being up is a reason to commit, not to back off — as long as his Fury is spent.

playing.title: Suppression beats his escape
playing.detail: Once Show Stopper lands, his E cannot get him out of it. That is your kill window at 6.

playing.title: Lose the wave on purpose
playing.detail: He shoves with Q, so let him. Farm under tower and don't contest a wave you don't need. Every minute you deny him a kill moves the game toward the half you win.
